title: pvSlice
body:
## pvSlice

ParaView's general Slice filter: cuts any dataset (or hyper tree grid) with an implicit surface (Plane, Box, Sphere or Cylinder) and returns polygonal data, i.e. surfaces from volumes and lines from surfaces, with point data interpolated. SliceOffsetValues produces several parallel copies of the cut surface in one node, and Crinkle slice instead keeps the whole input cells crossed by the surface. Use slice for a simple plane with Schemaxis defaults, pvSliceWithPlane for a faster multithreaded plane cut, or pvAxisAlignedSlice for hyper tree grids.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Unless set, the plane origin and normal are ParaView's initial values, which may depend on the input bounds; set SliceType options explicitly for reproducible cuts.
- For Sphere, Cylinder and Box slice types an offset is a value of the implicit function, not a distance; see SliceOffsetValues.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `Slice`. Identity: `filters/Cut`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Slice filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet); hyper-tree grids (adaptive AMR-like trees) (vtkHyperTreeGrid). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet","vtkHyperTreeGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Crinkleslice` | This parameter controls whether to extract the entire cells that are sliced by the region or just extract a triangulated surface of that region. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `HyperTreeGridSlicer` | This property sets the parameters of the slice function. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Axis Aligned Plane","Plane"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Axis Aligned Plane"}` |
| `PointMergeMethod` | This property specifies which incremental point locator to use for handling duplicate/coincident points. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Not Merging Points","Octree Binning","Uniform Binning"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Uniform Binning"}` |
| `SliceOffsetValues` | The values in this property specify a list of current offset values. This can be used to create multiple slices with different centers. Each entry represents a new slice with its center shifted by the offset value. The 'Values Range' information is the range based on the global bounding box, not necessarily on the current slice geometry configuration. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1]` |
| `SliceType` | This property sets the parameters of the slice function. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Box","Cylinder","Plane","Sphere"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Box"}` |
| `Triangulatetheslice` | This parameter controls whether to produce triangles in the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `UseDual` | If checked, uses the dual of the hyper tree grid. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

### Nested `HyperTreeGridSlicer` → `Axis Aligned Plane`

Syntax: `{"type":"Axis Aligned Plane","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Axis Aligned Plane`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HyperTreeGridSlicer.options.AlwaysSnapToNearestAxis` | When true, ParaView replaces Normal by the coordinate axis of its largest absolute component, so the plane is always perpendicular to x, y or z. The snapped normal is always positive ([-1, 0, 0] becomes [1, 0, 0]), and tied components are all set to 1 ([1, 1, 0] stays [1, 1, 0]) rather than resolved to one axis. When false, Normal is used as given. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `HyperTreeGridSlicer.options.Normal` | Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `HyperTreeGridSlicer.options.Offset` | Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `HyperTreeGridSlicer.options.Origin` | A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |

| `HyperTreeGridSlicer.options.Origin` | A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |

### Nested `PointMergeMethod` → `Not Merging Points`

Syntax: `{"type":"Not Merging Points","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `incremental_point_locators/NonMergingPointLocator`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Divisions` | Bucket counts along x, y and z inherited from the uniform point locator. Points are inserted without any duplicate search, so this has no effect on the output. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Numberofpointsperbucket` | Average bucket occupancy inherited from the uniform point locator; with direct insertion it has no effect on the output. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Nested `PointMergeMethod` → `Octree Binning`

Syntax: `{"type":"Octree Binning","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `incremental_point_locators/IncrementalOctreeMergePoints`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Maxnumberofpointsperleaf` | Maximum number of points an octree leaf holds before it is split into eight children. Smaller values build a deeper tree (more construction work, quicker searches inside each leaf); larger values do the opposite. Affects speed and memory only. | `{"maximum":256,"minimum":16,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `16` |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Tolerance` | Distance within which a new point is treated as an existing one and merged. ParaView fixes it at 0 for this choice and hides it, as its XML instructs (always zero for merging); a positive value would also merge distinct points closer than this distance, altering the geometry. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Nested `PointMergeMethod` → `Uniform Binning`

Syntax: `{"type":"Uniform Binning","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `incremental_point_locators/MergePoints`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Divisions` | Number of buckets along x, y and z of the uniform search grid used to find coincident points. It affects speed and memory only, never which points merge (only identical coordinates merge). VTK’s automatic sizing is on by default for this locator and ParaView does not expose it, so whenever the operation supplies an estimated point count the grid is sized from Number of points per bucket instead and Divisions is not used. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Numberofpointsperbucket` | Target average number of points per bucket when the bucket grid is sized automatically (bucket count = estimated point count / this value). Smaller values create more, smaller buckets. Affects speed and memory only. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Nested `SliceType` → `Box`

Syntax: `{"type":"Box","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Box`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SliceType.options.Bounds` | Reference box [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] used only when UseReferenceBounds is true; the box is then these bounds scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation and translated by Position, all about the coordinate origin, so Length [1, 1, 1], Rotation [0, 0, 0] and Position [0, 0, 0] reproduce Bounds exactly. Ignored otherwise. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":6,"minItems":6,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` |
| `SliceType.options.Length` | With UseReferenceBounds false: edge lengths [Lx, Ly, Lz] of the box along its own axes (ParaView applies them as scale factors to a unit cube). With UseReferenceBounds true: dimensionless scale factors applied to the Bounds box about the coordinate origin. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `SliceType.options.Position` | With UseReferenceBounds false: world coordinates [x, y, z] of the box’s minimum corner (before rotation); the box extends from Position to Position + Length along its own axes. With UseReferenceBounds true: a translation applied to the transformed Bounds box. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `SliceType.options.Rotation` | Rotation angles [rx, ry, rz] about the x, y and z axes, applied about the box’s local origin (its minimum corner at Position, not its centre; with UseReferenceBounds true, about the coordinate origin). The angles are combined in VTK’s Z-X-Y convention: the box transform is Translate · RotateZ · RotateX · RotateY · Scale. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `SliceType.options.UseReferenceBounds` | Chooses how the box is defined. False: the box is a unit cube scaled by Length, rotated about its corner and placed at Position. True: the box starts from Bounds, and Length, Rotation and Position act as scale, rotation and translation relative to it (about the coordinate origin). | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

### Nested `SliceType` → `Cylinder`

Syntax: `{"type":"Cylinder","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Cylinder`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SliceType.options.Axis` | Direction [ax, ay, az] of the cylinder's axis line through Center; the cylinder is infinitely long in both directions. For ordinary datasets ParaView normalizes the vector, so only its direction matters. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `SliceType.options.Center` | Any point [x, y, z] on the cylinder’s axis line. Moving it along Axis changes nothing; moving it sideways moves the cylinder. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `SliceType.options.Radius` | Distance from the axis line to the cylinder surface; points closer than this are inside. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SliceType.options.Normal` | Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `SliceType.options.Offset` | Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `SliceType.options.Origin` | A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |

### Nested `SliceType` → `Sphere`

Syntax: `{"type":"Sphere","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Sphere`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SliceType.options.Center` | Centre [x, y, z] of the sphere in the input’s coordinates; the region within Radius of this point is inside. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `SliceType.options.Radius` | Radius of the sphere: points closer than Radius to Center are inside. A larger radius encloses more of the data or moves the cut shell outward. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvSlice",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
